rationale: Acceptance lens did not run (no spec ArtifactRef; the Jira ACs in the task were not audited as business_review), so confidence is low; all 15 lens/standards candidates were reachability-checked within budget. Three blocking findings: Rule F also widens validate_run_files untested (AC2 scope), the icon lookup's leading-wildcard LIKE cannot use the btree icon_url index (impact unconfirmed), and a code-quality.md typing violation; 0 deferred, 12 dismissed as handled or speculative (e.g. SVG served via get_safe_svg_response, empty owner rejected by is_safe_blob_ref, no other get_by_icon_url callers).

standards_review.notes: both commit subjects in the range follow the git-workflow.md EPMCDME-####: Description format

new modules carry Apache headers and module cohesion holds; but get_by_icon_url in src/codemie/rest_api/models/assistant.py:1199 annotates its return as typing List['Assistant'] where code-quality.md prefers list[...]
no auth bypass, no secrets logged; icon lookup is a parameterized endswith with autoescape=True; Rule F needs an image mime, an assistant created by the file owner, and READ on it; lookup errors deny

findings.title: Use builtin list generic in get_by_icon_url
findings.problem: code-quality.md (Types And Imports) requires parameterized builtin generics such as list[str] in new code; the new public classmethod get_by_icon_url annotates its return as typing List['Assistant'].
findings.impact: code-quality.md is a blocking project standard and the standards audit marks code-quality partial because of this new public signature.
findings.recommendation: Annotate the return as list['Assistant'] instead of typing List['Assistant'], per code-quality.md Types And Imports (and drop List from the typing import if nothing else uses it).

findings.title: Icon lookup does an unindexed table scan
findings.problem: get_by_icon_url now matches icon_url with endswith('/v1/files/<token>'), i.e. LIKE '%...<token>' (two variants OR'ed). The only index is the btree ix_assistants_icon_url, which cannot serve a leading-wildcard pattern, so every call is a sequential scan of assistants. Rule F calls it for every image download not settled by Rules A-D2, before Rule E, so share-token image downloads also pay for it, and any authenticated requester can trigger it with arbitrary image tokens.
findings.impact: Each non-creator viewing an assistant list now fires one full assistants-table scan per displayed icon; cost grows with the table and with traffic. Realistic latency impact on production table size was not confirmed (reachability of the hot path is confirmed, magnitude is not).
findings.recommendation: Make the lookup index-servable: e.g. add a trigram (pg_trgm GIN) or reverse/expression index over icon_url, or persist the icon file token in its own indexed column and match by equality. At minimum keep Rule F as cheap as possible (it currently runs before Rule E, so share-token image downloads also pay for it).

findings.title: Rule F silently widens run-file validation
findings.problem: Rule F lives inside can_download, which validate_run_files also calls, so a user can now pass another user's image token as a workflow run file whenever a readable assistant created by that owner uses it as icon_url. No test covers this (all run-file test tokens are application/pdf, so Rule F exits at its mime check) and the validate_run_files docstring still says only Rule E does not apply.
findings.impact: The task's AC2 requires no file access broader than the assistant icon_url use case; accepting the icon as a run file (and registering it as workspace metadata via sync_uploaded_files) goes beyond it. Whether that registration yields lasting access after assistant READ is lost was not confirmed (Rule D only keys on workspace- owners), but the widening itself is live and unpinned.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether Rule F should apply outside GET /v1/files. Either scope it to the download route (e.g. a flag on can_download that validate_run_files leaves off) to keep AC2's 'no broader access' guarantee, or keep it and add a test in tests/codemie/service/test_agent_workspace_service_run_files.py with an image/png token owned by another user plus a readable assistant created by that owner, pinning the outcome, and update the validate_run_files docstring.
